narrative:
On August 17, 2026, the Karnataka High Court listed 3,134 cases across 48 benches and heard 1,301 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 41.5%. This marks an increase in both total caseload and overall efficiency compared to previous sessions, rising from 36.8% (950 of 2,580 heard) on August 14 and 38.5% (1,011 of 2,628 heard) on August 13.

Stage-wise progression was led by Orders, which comprised the largest share with 1,109 scheduled cases (35.3% heard). Final Hearings saw improved throughput, converting 25.7% of 623 scheduled matters compared to 17.7% on August 14. Admissions achieved a 42.6% hearing rate across 476 cases, while Further Hearings and Preliminary Hearings recorded strong conversions of 55.9% and 50.8%, respectively. By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket with 1,494 listings, improving to a 35.5% hearing rate from 29.7% on August 14. Criminal matters demonstrated robust clearance, with Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) converting 56.2% of 464 cases and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reaching 62.8%. In contrast, Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) clearance moderated to 36.4% from 50.1% on August 14.

Bench performance highlights included Justice M. Nagaprasanna, who heard 210 matters across two cause lists totaling 344 cases (achieving 57.5% and 66.0% hearing rates). Justice S Vishwajith Shetty addressed substantial volume, hearing 135 of 312 scheduled matters (43.3%). Notable conversion efficiencies were also achieved by Justice M.G.S. Kamal (76.7% of 43 cases heard) and Justice V Srishananda (65.9% of 88 cases heard).
